title: Derived Hom and the boundary of a two-term complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $d:M\to F$ be a morphism, and let $G$ be an object of $\mathcal A$. Regard $K=[M\xrightarrow d F]$ as a cochain complex in degrees $-1,0$, and objects of $\mathcal A$ as complexes in degree zero. Write $\operatorname{Ext}^n(K,G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(K,G[n])$. The quotient chain map $q:K\to M[1]$ induces an additive map
$$\partial:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^1(K,G),\qquad \delta\longmapsto\delta[1]\circ q.$$
The sequence
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(F,G)\xrightarrow{\theta\mapsto\theta d}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,G)\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Ext}^1(K,G)$$
is exact at its middle term. These maps commute with postcomposition by $G\to G'$ and with the induced maps from commutative squares between differentials $d$. Moreover the canonical chain map $K\to\operatorname{coker}(d)[0]$ induces a natural additive isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\operatorname{coker}(d),G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}^0(K,G)$. No projectivity or injectivity assumption on $M,F,G$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological) applied to the triangle F[0] -> K -> M[1] -> F[1], and Tag 06XS (lemma-negative-exts), clause (1), for Ext^0.

proof.text: Use the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cone of $d:M[0]\to F[0]$ is exactly $K$: its only nonzero differential is $d$ in degree $-1$. Its distinguished cone triangle is $M[0]\xrightarrow d F[0]\xrightarrow i K\xrightarrow{-q}M[1]$. By TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], rotating gives $(F[0],K,M[1];i,-q,-d[1])$. The identity on the first two vertices and $-1$ on the third identify this triangle with $F[0]\xrightarrow i K\xrightarrow q M[1]\xrightarrow{d[1]}F[1]$. Thus the latter triangle is distinguished. This sign calculation fixes the quotient $q$ occurring in the statement, rather than an unspecified connecting map.

Suppose $\partial(\delta)=\delta[1]q=0$. Apply clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] to the distinguished triangle of step 1 and $W=G[1]$. It gives $k:F[1]\to G[1]$ with $\delta[1]=k\,d[1]$. The shift is an autoequivalence, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies maps $F[0]\to G[0]$ with actual morphisms of $\mathcal A$. Hence $k=\theta[1]$ for a unique $\theta:F\to G$, and faithfulness of shift and of the single-complex embedding gives $\delta=\theta d$. Conversely, $d[1]q:K\to F[1]$ is null-homotopic: the only nonzero homotopy component is $h^0=1_F:K^0\to F[1]^{-1}$; its degree $-1$ component $h^0d=d$ is precisely that of $d[1]q$, and all remaining components are zero. It is therefore zero in $D(\mathcal A)$, so $\partial(\theta d)=0$. This proves exactness. Shift and composition are additive, so $\partial$ is additive.

source.place: Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), with the cone and homotopy-category localization conventions

proof.text: Put $C=\operatorname{coker}(d)$, $I=\operatorname{im}(d)$, and $L=[M\twoheadrightarrow I]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The componentwise kernel of the canonical map $p:K\to C[0]$ is $L$, so $0\to L\to K\xrightarrow p C[0]\to0$ is degreewise short exact: in degree zero it is $0\to I\to F\to C\to0$, and in degree $-1$ it is $0\to M\xrightarrow1 M\to0\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this yields a distinguished triangle $L\to K\xrightarrow p C[0]\to L[1]$. No splitting of $M\twoheadrightarrow I$ or $F\twoheadrightarrow C$ is required.

The differential $M\twoheadrightarrow I$ is epic, so $H^j(L)=0$ for every $j\ge0$; also $H^j(L[1])=H^{j+1}(L)=0$ for $j\ge-1$. Consequently $L\in D(\mathcal A)^{\le-1}$ and $L[1]\in D(\mathcal A)^{\le-2}\subset D(\mathcal A)^{\le-1}$, while $G[0]\in D(\mathcal A)^{\ge0}$. The standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and shifted orthogonality axiom (2) of [def-weil-t-structure] give $\operatorname{Hom}(L,G[0])=\operatorname{Hom}(L[1],G[0])=0$. Explicitly for $U=L$ or $L[1]$, take $A=U[-1]\in D^{\le0}$ and $B=G[0]\in D^{\ge0}$ in $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[-1])=0$ and shift both arguments by $[1]$.

source.place: Tag 06XS (lemma-negative-exts), clause (1), vanishing argument via the standard t-structure

proof.text: Apply clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] to the triangle of step 3: since every $L\to G[0]$ is zero, every $a:K\to G[0]$ factors as $b p$ with $b:C[0]\to G[0]$. If $b p=b\prime p$, clause (ii) applied to $b-b\prime$ factors this difference through $L[1]$, and the second vanishing of step 4 makes it zero. Thus $p^*$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(C[0],G[0])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(K,G[0])$. It is additive, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies its source with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(C,G)$; this is exactly the asserted map induced by the canonical chain map $p$. A bijective additive map has additive inverse, giving the required additive isomorphism.

For $g:G\to G\prime$, associativity and functoriality of shift give $g[1](\delta[1]q)=(g\delta)[1]q$. For a commutative square $b d=d\prime a$ with $a:M\to M\prime$, $b:F\to F\prime$, its chain map $u:K\to K\prime$ has components $a,b$ and satisfies $q\prime u=a[1]q$. Hence $\partial_d(\delta\prime a)=\partial_{d\prime}(\delta\prime)u$, while $(\theta\prime b)d=\theta\prime d\prime a$ proves naturality of the preceding arrow. The induced cokernel map $c:C\to C\prime$ is characterized by $c\pi=\pi\prime b$, so $p\prime u=c[0]p$ componentwise. For $\gamma:C\prime\to G$, this gives $(\gamma c)[0]p=\gamma[0]p\prime u$, and postcomposition likewise gives $g[0]\gamma[0]p=(g\gamma)[0]p$. These equations prove naturality of the additive isomorphism, including its inverse by uniqueness. All constructions used only abelianness and the derived-category structure, never enough projectives or injectives.
